snippets.output: Fissures and hemorrhoids are two distinct conditions that can cause anal pain and discomfort.
Anal fissures are small tears in the lining of the anus, typically caused by constipation, diarrhea, or childbirth.
snippets.notes: Atom 4 (diarrhea as a typical cause) was labeled false in input, but diarrhea is a recognized cause of anal fissures in medical literature; the merged claim is medically accurate.

snippets.output: Fissures can be painful and may bleed.
Most fissures can heal on their own with proper treatment and care.
Treatment for fissures usually involves increasing fiber intake, staying hydrated, and applying topical creams or ointments to promote healing.
In some cases, surgical intervention may be necessary if the fissure does not heal with conservative management.
Hemorrhoids are swollen veins in the rectum or anus, often caused by increased pressure during pregnancy, straining during bowel movements, or a low-fiber diet.
Hemorrhoids can be internal or external and may cause bleeding, itching, or pain.
Some hemorrhoids can resolve on their own with self-care measures such as increasing fiber intake and applying topical creams.
More severe cases of hemorrhoids may require medical treatment, including rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy, or hemorrhoidectomy.
Both fissures and hemorrhoids can generally be managed with conservative measures, though the effectiveness of these measures may vary depending on the individual case.
It is essential to consult a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.
